text:
marta: Quick sync — we need final copy for the competitive battlecard ahead of Thurs webinar + launch posts. Focus: cloud AI platforms, LLM API providers, and infra vendors. Need: 3 top claims + 1-line proof each, 2 inbound hooks for SDRs, and one slide for webinar. Can we converge today?

shannon: I'm thinking claim structure = claim / evidence / customer impact. Short and punchy. Example: 'Predictable inference economics' / 'autoscaling reserved pools + batching saved X% in our tests' / 'reduces cost per convo for merchant apps' — want concrete wording.

ana: +1 to structure. For evidence we should avoid absolute competitor numbers but point to our features: Dedicated capacity SLA, private VPC option, and per-route cost analytics.

ana: Proposed top-3 claims draft: 
1) "Consistent production performance across hosted, dedicated, and private" — proof: "SLA-backed dedicated pools + smart routing that falls back to compatible variants." 
2) "Better unit economics for conversational workloads" — proof: "batching + prefix KV caching reduces per-token cost; Optimize recommendations cut infra spend in trials." 
3) "Enterprise deployment & compliance without forklift infra" — proof: "Private control plane, KMS/HSM + audit logs; deploy on-prem or in VPC."

priya: Love those. For the webinar slide we should pair each claim with an objection & response. Example: Objection: 'Cloud vendor has scale' -> Response: 'Scale != predictable latency or cost; our routing + reserved pools give predictable P95 and fallback behavior.'

shannon: Can we add one benchmarking datapoint that is defensible? Suggest: "In our internal conversational benchmark (8k context mix), median inference latency decreased by ~30% when using dedicated pools + batching vs a baseline shared-hosted setup." Keep it high-level, no competitor names.

marta: Yes keep competitor names out of the slide copy. But SDRs need quick callouts versus cloud platforms + LLM APIs + infra vendors. Draft routing hooks: 
- For cloud AI platform leads: "Looking for predictable latency and unit economics beyond raw capacity? Let's show a 1-page economics comparison."
- For LLM API leads: "Need more control over model variants, rollouts, and private deployments? Demo of Dedicated + Private in 30m."

ana: Also add a short rebuttal vs infra vendors that sell self-hosted runtimes: "We give the same low-level controls but with the ops tooling and SLAs so product teams don't have to hire a dedicated infra team."

priya: Two inbound subject lines for webinar / launch email + quick AB variants: 
A1: "How to get production-grade LLM inference without re-architecting your stack"
A2: "Reduce inference cost and guarantee latency for LLM apps — 30 minute demo"
B1: "Benchmarks that matter: latency, cost, and enterprise controls"
B2: "Stop trading reliability for cost: inference that scales predictably"

shannon: For the battlecard one-pager, recommended sections: 1) Claim bullets (3), 2) Quick proofs (2 lines each), 3) Rebuttals (top 4 objections), 4) Routing hooks, 5) One sentence customer story (anonymized).

marta: Who can draft the one-pager? Need a first pass by EOD to pass to SDR lead. @ana can you take initial draft?

ana: I can. Will produce a concise one-pager (single slide) with the claims, proofs, 4 rebuttals, and two inbound hooks. Posting link when done: https://redwood.internal/briefs/competitive-bc-draft (will update).

priya: Quick phrasing nit: change 'unit economics' phrasing for external copy to 'cost per conversation' — more tangible to customers.

shannon: Agreed. Also add one example metric line for the slide: 'Typical production setup: 20–40% savings on token cost with batching + caching for chat workloads.' (framed as 'typical' not guaranteed).

marta: Great. Final checklist: 
- Ana: one-pager draft by EOD (confirmed)
- Marketing: 2 subject lines + 2 short social hooks for launch (I'll do)
- Growth/SDR: confirm routing rules for cloud vs api vs infra leads (Pria, can you confirm?)
- Legal: quick claims review (I'll ping them)

priya: I'll map the routing triggers today and post the doc. Quick question — do we want a lightweight playbook for the SDRs covering the 4 common objections? If yes I'll add 3 quick scripts.

marta: Yes please — 3 scripts + 1 escalation checklist. Keep scripts 1–2 lines.

devops-bot: Deploy reminder: webinar landing page scheduled deploy at 2026-04-02T16:00Z. CI pipeline will run 03:30 UTC smoke tests.

shannon: Perfect. If everyone is aligned I'll consolidate language after Ana posts the draft and push to the shared drive. :thumbsup: 

ana: Draft posted: https://redwood.internal/briefs/competitive-bc-draft (comments welcome). Will iterate on phrasing for public copy.

marta: Thanks all — team standby for final copy review at 4pm PT.
